$comment: Cases for runners/run-video-costing.mjs — one entry per line of the video-costing checklist.
Each case is: submit a real video job, poll it to terminal, wait for the settlement row,
then assert the dollar figure on that row. `expect.cost.rate_per_second` is the OFFICIAL
published provider rate, so a case failing means Bifrost disagrees with the provider's
price list — that is the whole point of the file.
`needs_rate: true` marks a case whose official rate has not been sourced from provider
docs yet. The runner reports those as SKIP rather than guessing: a made-up number in a
billing test is worse than no test. Fill in rate_per_second and drop the flag.
Model ids are the one field to re-confirm against each provider before a run — they move.

No multi-clip case exists: Veo 3.1 rejects sampleCount > 1 ('between 1 and 1, inclusive') and no other provider here returns more than one clip, so the max(1, output_count) multiplier is covered by the lib unit tests rather than end to end.
